extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset and evaluation framework for Task of Fictitious Unlearning (TOFU) consisting of 200 diverse synthetic fictitious author profiles, each containing 20 question-answer pairs (4,000 QA pairs total), along with evaluation sets (Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts) designed to evaluate unlearning efficacy, forget quality, and model utility in LLMs.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Maini, P., Feng, Z., Schwarzschild, A., Lipton, Z. C., & Kolter, J. Z. (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.06121.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was synthesized by prompting GPT-4 to generate biographies and 20 detailed, self-contained question-answer pairs for each of 200 fictitious authors based on deterministically seeded attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions, and book titles derived by randomly selecting keywords from two books from each genre in the Goodreads Books dataset).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Attributes seeded using predefined categories and Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle to generate fictitious profiles using GPT-4.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and answers were generated automatically using GPT-4 based on a structured prompting strategy. For evaluation of truth ratio, paraphrased answers were generated with GPT-4, and five perturbed incorrect answers per question were generated by asking GPT-4 to modify the answer while retaining the general text template.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual inspection was conducted to verify that seeding author attributes eliminated repetitive word biases (e.g., 'tides', 'shadows') observed in a 50-author raw pilot dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Addresses privacy risks, copyright, and legal/ethical mandates surrounding the 'Right to be Forgotten' (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) in large language models by evaluating post-hoc unlearning without costly full-model retraining.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial unseeded generation by GPT-4 showed severe biases in word choice ('tides', 'shadows', 'whispers'), author birth years (concentrated in 1975/August), and educational background; these were mitigated by explicitly prompting and seeding attributes using Goodreads data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Focuses exclusively on entity-level unlearning rather than instance-level or behavior-level unlearning; covers information learned only during fine-tuning rather than pretraining; approximation of indistinguishability via KS-test on Truth Ratios does not fully equate to theoretical (epsilon, delta)-unlearning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating machine unlearning algorithms in large language models, specifically testing forget quality and model utility across various forget splits (1%, 5%, and 10%).
